normalized.title: ESEC-2 FLIGHT OPERATIONS SERVICE CONTRACT
normalized.description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements.  ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are:  Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions")  Perform its In-Orbit activities.  Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations:   A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. The Small Satellites Mission Operations Centre is therefore responsible of the monitoring and control of the satellite and the corresponding ground segment, the handling of the user requests, the extraction of the mission products and their availability for distribution.  The Small Satellites operations concept relies on a highly automatic functioning of the ground segment and a high degree of autonomy in the space segment for the delayed execution of operations requested by telecommand and for satellite survival. No operator attended shift work is foreseen. Operational engineers supervise the small satellites mission operations and related performances usually only during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The satellites are safe by design and can survive for a long period without ground station contact.   This WP will cover OPSPREP and OPS activities, support to Industry, execution of delegated tasks for critical operations (LEOP, others) together and in collaboration with Industry for this small satellite missions. This WP may implement further mission operations engineering activities carried out in support of other ESA programmes requested by ESA programme directorates to OPS. WP-2 Galileo Hosting activities:  The Galileo Hosting support will be provided in response to the requirements and agreements reached with EUSPA for Galileo and EGNOS. The provision of support to the hosting and testing activities will be performed on-site during normal working hours. Provisions for an On-Call service shall be also considered for the WP. Occasional working outside normal working hours and overtime may be required. The Agency will issue one single Invitation to Tender in Open Competition for the two WPs. Considering the relatively small volume covered by this procurement, the Tenderers will be invited to provide a single proposal covering the support to both areas.   The new contract is planned to be kicked-off starting in 1st Quarter 2027 (phase-in) as required to permit sufficient time for a smooth transition (e.g. training, certification of new service provider's personnel).  The operational phase of the contract is expected to start latest by 2nd Quarter 2027, at the expiry of the current INDUSTRIAL SERVICE PROVISION IN SUPPORT OF THE OPERATION OF ESA IN BELGIUM contract extension.

normalized.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-1-a5d320e5fd3b501c76756c8c2a2b3a8ff968f4c44b94565e158858ff4f81f4b4.json","sha256":"a5d320e5fd3b501c76756c8c2a2b3a8ff968f4c44b94565e158858ff4f81f4b4","row":8,"retrievedAt":"2026-11-09T09:32:29.357Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000046321","closingDate":"2026-12-18T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-12-11T13:00:00","description":"Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). normalized.title: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS
normalized.description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. normalized.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a highly integrated and efficient millimetre-wave phased array antenna using advanced packaging solution for multi-chip,multi-technology assembly, including 3-dimensional heterogeneous integration interconnects, thermal and power management.Targeted Improvements:Enabling disruptive technology to enable thermal management of highly integrated phased arrays, with a twice the RF power handling capability.Description: The development and deployment of millimetre-wave phased array antennas present several challenges that can reduce their efficiency and performance. These challenges include low RF power per element across different orbits (Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Geostationary EarthOrbit (GEO)) due to the use of silicon chips and the inefficiency in thermal management. Further limitations are introduced by the use of 2D packaging, which prevents the integration of high-power handling capabilities and enhanced thermal management technologies.The power efficiency and dependability of the antenna are reduced by signal strength degradation caused by the low RF output power per element. These performance issues directly affect satellite-to-ground communication as well as intersatellite communication.Toovercome these limitations, transitioning from 2D to 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI) interconnect technology can significantly improve the thermal and power performance of phased array antennas. By stacking components vertically, more space can be allocated for effective thermal management, and the integration of multiple layers with thermal vias allows for better heat dissipation. This approach also enables the integration of diverse materials and technologies within the same package. Novel materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) offer superior thermal conductivity and higher power handling capabilities compared to traditional silicon. Incorporating thesematerials into the antenna array, using an Integrated Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) approach, can increase the RF power per element while alleviating thermal constraints.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 will develop an antenna concept, investigate and develop key processes necessary to fabricate a millimetre-wave 3DHI active antenna.This includes integrating low-power silicon chips, RF power amplifiers, thermal management solutions and advanced packaging techniques. During this phase, critical components will be developed to breadboard level to assess the effectiveness of 3D packaging methods, such as vertical integration and thermal vias, in addressing thermal dissipation and RF power handling challenges. Phase 1 outputwill deliver an antenna concept supported by critical breadboard test results. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 1,000 kEuro.- Phase2 will focus on developing a scaled engineering model of a millimetre-wave phased array antenna using 3DHI technology in Q, V, orW-Bands.
